His parents liked him home before dark and wanted to know where he was going. The school expected students on trips to stay in groups. A film for two was out. More than that, he did not want Preeti to feel cornered. So: the museum trip, daytime, six or seven classmates, and he would tell Mummy that Preeti was in the group. subtype: Approach: considering family rules and school norms [Thinking]
passage: Francis wanted to ask Minakshi to go somewhere after the Class 11 exams, but first he sat at his desk in the Bengaluru flat and thought about the details. His parents didn't mind him having friends who were girls, but they'd want to know where he was. Minakshi's family was stricter; she had once said she wasn't allowed out after dark. And the school had a rule about students meeting off campus during school hours. So: not a school day, not evening, not just the two of them. A group trip to the science museum on Saturday afternoon, with Joel and Anita coming too. That way she could tell her parents honestly, he could tell his, and nobody would be stuck feeling awkward. He told his mother at dinner. "A group, in the daytime. Sounds sensible," she said.

qa.q: Where did Francis plan the group trip?
qa.a: To the science museum on Saturday afternoon.

qa.q: Why did Francis think about Minakshi's family before asking?
qa.a: He felt careful and considerate, not wanting her to be uncomfortable or in trouble, since her family was stricter.

qa.q: What makes the museum plan a thoughtful choice?
qa.a: It is daytime, in a group and on a weekend, so it fits both families' rules, lets both be honest at home and keeps things comfortable.

qa.q: How might Minakshi feel about the plan?
qa.a: Minakshi could feel relieved and respected, able to say yes without going against her family or hiding anything.

grounding: Shows a student weighing family expectations and school rules and choosing a daytime group outing he can be honest about.

"I want to ask Aakash to the fest," Nikita said, lying on Pooja's bed. "Just the two of us."
"Your parents will be fine with that?"
Nikita made a face. "Mummy would ask a hundred questions. And the fest ends at nine."
"And Aakash's family?"
"He said once his dad drops him everywhere." Nikita sat up. "Okay. So maybe not just the two of us, and not at night."
"What about the afternoon events? There's the quiz and the music thing at three."
"With you and Farhan and a few others?"
"Then you can tell your mummy the truth. And he won't feel weird either."
Nikita thought. "Honestly, I'd feel more relaxed in a group too."
"So ask him to the three o'clock quiz. Group team."
"Group team," Nikita said, and started typing.

qa.q: How did Nikita feel about going as a group in the end?
qa.a: She realised she would feel more relaxed in a group, which eased her worry about her mother's questions.

qa.q: Why is the three o'clock group quiz a good plan?
qa.a: It is daytime and in a group, so Nikita can be honest with her mother and Aakash can feel comfortable too.

qa.q: How might Aakash feel being invited to a group quiz team?
qa.a: Aakash is likely to feel at ease, since it is a friendly group activity rather than a pressured one-on-one date.
